name: Simple Interest Foundations and Time Units
description: Build the meaning of principal, interest, rate, time, and amount, then calculate simple interest mentally across years, months, and exact day counts.
script_scope: Teach simple interest as a fixed yearly rent on the original principal. Introduce P, R, T, S.I., and Amount, but derive the formula from one-year interest before using it. Cover months, mixed years-and-months, and the chapter's day-count convention that excludes the deposit day and includes the withdrawal day. Distinguish interest from amount and emphasise cancellation and benchmark percentages for mental calculation. End with mixed time-unit amount questions.

name: Finding Principal, Rate, Time, and Amount
description: Reverse the simple-interest relationship confidently to recover whichever quantity is missing.
script_scope: Teach the four-way reversal of S.I. = PRT/100: finding principal, rate, time, and amount. Include amount-first questions where S.I. must first be found as A−P, growth-factor questions A=P(1+RT/100), reverse questions with months, and proportional shortcuts when only rate changes. Emphasise identifying the missing quantity before calculating and checking the result forward in the original relation.

name: Amount Differences and Constant Yearly Interest
description: Exploit the fact that simple-interest amounts rise by the same rupee amount every year to solve two-date questions quickly.
script_scope: Teach the linear-growth nature of simple interest: the difference between amounts at two times equals the interest for the gap. Use this to find one-year interest, principal, rate, and amounts at new times without repeatedly applying the full formula. Include proportional scaling across time, scaling to a new principal under the same rate-time conditions, and two-amount capstones that recover both principal and rate.

name: Doubling, Trebling, and Interest as a Fraction of Principal
description: Turn amount multiples and principal fractions into fast rate-time relationships without needing the actual principal.
script_scope: Teach that doubling means S.I.=P, trebling means S.I.=2P, and in general an amount multiple converts to an interest multiple. Cover rate/time shortcuts for doubling and trebling, S.I. given as a fraction or percentage of principal, the pattern where rate percent and time are numerically equal, and comparison of rates from different amount-multiple statements. Emphasise cancelling P before doing arithmetic.

name: Changing Rates and Principal Across Time
description: Split multi-stage simple-interest problems into clean time blocks when rates or the outstanding principal change.
script_scope: Cover piecewise rates for different year ranges, rates that change each year, principal added or withdrawn midway, equal-amount comparisons with different rate-time schedules, and the shortcut for extra interest caused by a rate increase. Teach that each block is still simple interest on the active principal for that block; the results are added, not compounded.

name: Comparing Interest Deals and Difference Shortcuts
description: Compare rates, times, principals, and borrowing/lending deals using proportionality instead of restarting the full calculation each time.
script_scope: Teach interest differences caused by rate changes or time changes, equal-interest conditions across different rate-time or principal-rate-time combinations, borrowing at one rate and lending at another, and recovering principal from a change in yearly income. Emphasise comparing the product P×R×T and cancelling common factors whenever possible.

name: Splitting Capital and Weighted Interest
description: Divide a total investment across different rates and use weighted-average reasoning to recover missing parts or rates.
script_scope: Teach two-part and three-part investment splits, total yearly income equations, weighted average rate, equal-interest deposit ratios, fixed-fraction allocations, unknown component rates, and alligation-style shortcuts for an overall rate. Emphasise that an overall rate is a weighted average and must lie between the component rates.

name: Equal Interest and Equal Amount Ratios
description: Use PRT products and amount factors to compare investments designed to produce equal interest or equal maturity values.
script_scope: Teach P1R1T1=P2R2T2 for equal simple interest, inverse RT principal ratios, equal-sum interest differences, three-scheme equal-interest ratios, and equal-final-amount problems using amount factors 1+RT/100. Include the chapter's algebraic relation y²=xz when successive interests are calculated under the same rate and time. End with multi-part equal-interest allocations.

name: Present Worth, Loans, and Repayments
description: Apply simple interest to future dues, loan settlement, part payments, down payments, and borrowing/lending decisions.
script_scope: Teach present worth through A=P(1+RT/100), ordinary loan repayment, part-payment timelines, cash down payments where only the unpaid balance earns interest, net gain from borrowing at one rate and lending at another, and rate recovery from a known repayment amount. Keep the source's simple-interest treatment explicit and separate principal from accumulated interest at every stage.

name: Instalments and Simple-Interest Finance Plans
description: Value equal instalments at a common date and understand why payment timing matters in debt and finance-plan questions.
script_scope: Teach equal annual instalments for a debt due at a future date, the accumulated-value method used by the chapter, monthly instalment schedules, down payments, financed balance, finance charge, and the source's month-weight method for recovering an annual simple-interest rate. Emphasise that instalments paid at different times cannot be treated as if they were all outstanding for the full term.

name: Data Sufficiency for Simple Interest
description: Decide whether one statement, the other, either one, both together, or neither can uniquely determine a simple-interest quantity.
script_scope: Teach the chapter's five-outcome two-statement data-sufficiency format and extend to three-statement combinations. Use rate, principal, amount, doubling, split-investment, and interest-difference situations. Emphasise testing I alone, II alone, and only then both; distinguish redundant information from genuinely independent equations; and flag cases where multiple P,R,T combinations remain possible.
